note: THE BOUNDS RULE, MEASURED RATHER THAN PREDICTED, and it is not the `out-of-range bounds raise' this phase's plan expected. Emacs answers (t -4 (args-out-of-range "abc" 5 3) -1 (args-out-of-range "abc" -5 3) -1). An END past the string is CLIPPED and is not an error -- (compare-strings "abc" 0 10 ...) is `t', and the second element shows the clip is real rather than lucky: "abc" 0..4 against "abcd" 0..4 compares three characters and then runs out, -4. A START past the string IS `args-out-of-range', and the data echoes the CLIPPED end ("abc" 5 3), not the 6 that was passed. A NEGATIVE index counts from the end -- -1 over "abc" is 2, so only "c" is compared and the answer is -1 -- and one that reaches past the start is the same range error. The fifth element is the pair the other four make attributable: -5 and 5 are both errors, -1 and 10 are both accepted. kg answers `void-function' at this pin. THIS CASE FLIPPED in the frontier demand phase, with the clip-and-raise rule implemented as measured rather than as the plan predicted it: END is clipped against the string's length before the range test, which is also why the error's data echoes the clip.
